Lines.Text: WHIRRR, CLACK. WHIRRR, CLACK.
An old fan rattled past the end of its useful life, coughing out damp, warm air.
The cramped office barely covered seven square meters. Across the gray walls and desk, steeped in the stale smell of the rainy season, patches of violent, vivid red had bloomed.
[SEIZED]
Scarlet death sentences left wherever the court officers' shoes had trampled.
Buried among those ugly papers, P slumped over his desk with his face in his hands.
Crumpled documents and printed emails lay scattered between his fingers like bloodstains.
[From: ABC Network Producer] Producer P, we have to pull the 'Dream Live' opening slot.
P, we have to cancel the opening slot on Dream Live. S-Tier has threatened to pull every one of their artists if we put your group onstage. Please refrain from contacting us for the time being.
[From: Songtan Local Festival Committee] Notice of contract cancellation. We will cover the penalty ourselves.
A year had passed since he had walked out after striking a defiant blow against the industry's giant.
P had believed his songs and the girls' hard work could pry open any door.
But the walls money built were tighter and crueler than he had imagined.
S-Tier had done more than throw the girls away. It had squeezed the air out of the entire industry.
Variety shows, music programs, even dusty stages at rural markets.
Rather than offend their golden goose, the people at the top of the networks had quietly chosen to choke off five unknown rookies.
For a year, no matter how good the songs were, every speaker that could carry them to the world had been ripped away.
The agency had burned through P's entire fortune on termination penalties and borrowed from private moneylenders on top of it. Now it stood on the edge of bankruptcy.
BZZT. BZZT.
His phone vibrated briefly, its screen webbed with cracks.
[Account Balance: ₩7,420]
Buy a few convenience-store meals for the girls tomorrow, and it would be gone.
P stared at the lifeless number with bloodshot eyes. Then a wounded, animal sound escaped him, and he seized his hair in both hands.
Had his grand, defiant choice only dragged the girls into the deepest darkness in the world? Self-loathing closed around his throat.
Then he heard it.
THUMP! TAP-TAP, THUMP—!!
Heavy impacts and rough scuffling carried through the thin plywood door.
P raised his reddened eyes and looked through a gap in the battered blinds.
With the amplifiers seized and unusable, a phone lying facedown on the floor supplied a tinny beat.
Over its ragged sound, five girls drenched in sweat drove their steps into the floor as though they meant to break it.
A red [SEIZED] sticker disfigured the center of the full-length mirror. It cut across their reflections, but their formation never wavered.
(breathing hard, picking out the flaw immediately) Seoyun. Your arm was off on that turn.
Don't use that hideous red sticker as an excuse to get sloppy. You should know your marks without a mirror.
(blowing her wet bangs off her forehead, feigning innocence) Okay, sorry, sorry. No, wait—hear me out.

(blowing her wet bangs off her forehead, feigning innocence) Okay, sorry, sorry. But hear me out. That sticker's dead center, right? Exactly between my eyebrows. It's blocking my third eye. How am I supposed to channel my energy with a giant red piece of paper jamming the signal? Of course I lost my bal—
(pressing her temples, letting out a long sigh) Ugh. You're killing me. Engage your core before I gouge out that third eye of yours. And stop shuffling. You're kicking up dust.
(completely unfazed, snapping a playful salute) Yes, ma'am! Spine upright at all times, lest I incur the wrath of Professor Mina!
Mina pressed a hand to her forehead, exasperated. But there was life in the sidelong look she gave Seoyun, and no real malice.
Her exacting perfectionism and Seoyun's irrepressible cheer kept the dark basement charged with energy.
(clapping to bring everyone back together) All right, you two. Focus! Jiwoo and I got a little tangled on that crossover.
I'll hold my breath half a beat longer. Jiwoo, come in on your usual count.
(nodding eagerly) No, Ria, I've got it!
I'll pull my toes in a little more. And Hana, your timing on that entrance was perfect!
(fidgeting, barely above a whisper) Mm... You were right in front of me, Jiwoo. Helping me catch the beat... I didn't lose the tempo. I can keep going.
(brushing dust from her clothes, smiling brightly) Good! P could bring us a gig any day.
We need this so ingrained we could wake up in the dark and dance it in our sleep. From the top! Three, four!
The music burst out again. Their eyes changed, and their bodies cut through the air.
Watching their fierce movements through the blinds, P felt his eyes brim.
A damp, airless basement on the verge of losing its electricity.
Faces hollowed by meals of instant noodles.
Yet there was barely a trace of doubt or despair in their eyes.
Among those terrible red marks, the girls danced with one unshakable faith: P had brought them out once, and he would lead them onto the brightest stage in the world.
The world could trample them and pretend they did not exist. Their dreams still burned in the dark.
His gaze caught on three crumpled thousand-won notes and a five-hundred-won coin at the corner of his desk.
The girls had quietly left the 3,500 won there the night before. Jiwoo had said it was their change from buying noodles.
They had so little, and still they had given up part of their share for him. The warmth of it weighed more than he could bear.
P slowly reached for the money.
The worn notes crumpled in his sweating fist.
If he fell apart, those girls really would have nowhere to go.
S-Tier's money could crash over them like a tidal wave. The world could close ranks like a fortress. He still had to be their shield—the only one they had—and the sword that cut a path for them.
The self-loathing receded from his bloodshot eyes. In its place rose a cold, fierce determination.
(pressing his clenched fist to his forehead, forcing the words through his teeth) Fine... Let's see who breaks first.
Even if I have to carve the flesh off my own bones... I'll get you a real stage. Somewhere you can finally breathe.
P shot to his feet and grabbed the crumpled jacket hanging over his chair.
His balance was still 7,420 won, and every rule in the world still had its hands around their throats.
But the girls' fierce breathing beyond that plywood wall straightened his bowed back once more.
He jammed his feet into his worn shoes and left the office, ready to throw himself against the industry's sealed walls again, whatever it cost him.
